applicable_when: XBLOCK=128 is applied to xnumel=9, meaning 119 out of 128 threads per X-tile are masked on every iteration. This wastes 93% of thread slots in the X dimension, produces uncoalesced global loads (only 18/32 bytes per sector utilized), and inflates the grid to 4096 blocks creating a 50% tail-effect partial wave across 132 SMs. The fix is to shrink XBLOCK to match xnumel (<=16) and grow YBLOCK (32-128) so the Y dimension (ynumel=32768) drives parallelism efficiently. This collapses the grid to ~256-1024 blocks, eliminates the partial wave, and aligns thread access patterns with the Y-stride memory layout for better coalescing.
